notes.title: DEVLOG #11 Networking Part 1 - Who’s Got The Crate?
notes.content:
[p]Hello! I’m one of the engineers on Begone Beast and this is the first in a series of posts about Networking and Multiplayer systems, which is where I spend a lot of my time and energy.  [/p][p]
One of the goals in multiplayer game development is making sure that the world each player sees is as consistent as possible for things that matter.  For this blog post, we wanted to share a simple yet amusing challenge that we needed to solve for our Throwables: if two players pick up an item at the same time, who gets to throw it at that large horde of hands?![/p][p][/p][h2]What’s a Throwable?[/h2][p][img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/43170231/8835d6e18587bcecac9712ed09a55a54a695b22d.png"][/img][/p][p]A Throwable is a game object like a crate or an oil drum that a player can pick up and fling at a bunch of enemies. We also have Deployables like barricades and turrets that players can use for strategy and crowd control.  And both of these are types of Pickupables in terms of game object hierarchy, but throwable is more fun to say so that’s what I’m going to use.[/p][p][/p][p]Let’s say there’s a crate in the level that two players want to pick up.  The first challenge is making sure the crate exists up in the same place in both players’ worlds, which Unity mostly handles for us.  When a player picks up a crate, it’s given to that player and removed from the world for everyone else.[/p][p][/p][p]But what happens when those two players try to pick up the same crate, at the same time?  This happens more often than you might think!  In the chaos of a battle, players are grabbing anything and everything they can, but because this information has to travel over the internet there is always a small  window of uncertainty.  [/p][p][/p][p][img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/43170231/eaeca35fa7ed51e89b6c9ed0e87ef4c76c734b7c.png"][/img][/p][h2]
Who’s Got the Crate?[/h2][p]In Begone Beast one of the players acts as the Host for the parts of the game that need a single source of truth.  The host is responsible for spawning network objects, executing abilities, running monster behaviors and, as it happens, deciding who picked up a throwable crate.[/p][p][/p][p]In the case of simultaneous pickup, a straightforward approach to deciding who actually grabbed the crate is just to have both players send a request to the host, then the host decides the winner (simply by whose request arrived first) and notifies both players of the outcome.[/p][p][/p][p][img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/43170231/04b61a2756f96c4ad0229eb1fcc95efbe575d3f8.png"][/img][/p][p][/p][p]This works but can make the UX feel sluggish because the winning player can’t actually perform any pickup actions until they hear back from the host.  That round trip communication takes time and is entirely dependent on the internet’s speed and mood.[/p][p][/p][h2]They Can’t Both Be Right, Right?[/h2][p]An alternative approach, and the one we use for Begone Beast, is for each player to [i]assume [/i]they have successfully picked up the object.  This way we can start playing pickup animations and the UX feels snappy and responsive.  But it does create another interesting situation: what happens to the player who didn’t really pick up the crate?  After all, the host still has to choose a winner.[/p][p]
[img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/43170231/239400c98d4acde91d86e22992b7638dacea4645.png"][/img][/p][p]In Begone Beast, both players will optimistically start their pickup animation while sending the pickup request to the host.  When the response comes back, the “losing” player will have to stop any pickup animation in progress and cancel any effects (including [i]proxy crates[/i]… but that’s a story for another day). Keep in mind this is all happening in just a few frames, but those frames really matter to make sure actions feel responsive.[/p][p][/p][p]It’s tricky to get right and can create a brief moment where you can start picking up a crate that another player got to first. But one of our guiding principles is to make your actions feel as responsive as possible. In this case the winning player already has the crate and the feedback was instantaneous, so we felt it was worth it.[/p][p][/p][p]Thanks for joining me on this trip around the internet!  As always, deep breath and …[/p][p][img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/43170231/3af2fc01c606c60d814042de453b2110a16a081e.png"][/img][/p]

notes.title: DEVLOG #10 The Effect Chain
notes.content:
[p]Hi all, Patrick on the engineering team here with a slightly more technical post![/p][p][/p][p]When making games, a lot of effort goes into making tools for the developers, both so that gameplay can be implemented as quickly and easily as possible, and so that non-programmers can more easily make changes to the gameplay.[/p][p][/p][p]One big system we’ve been working on in Begone Beast is the [b]effect chain[/b] system, which is our version of something similar to a [url="https://www.gamedeveloper.com/programming/behavior-trees-for-ai-how-they-work"][u]behavior tree[/u][/url]. We use this for our enemy behaviors, player abilities, and a number of other places.[/p][p][/p][p]Here’s an example of an effect chain for the behavior of some horde monsters:[/p][p][img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/43170231/500cd1ff6cb4eda3719bde058240613fbf34b85e.png"][/img][/p][p][i]Look at all those fancy boxes![/i][/p][hr][/hr][p][/p][p]I’ve collapsed most of the steps for simplicity, but you can see the general behavior flow from the comments. Find a target, run away if we’re afraid, attack the target if we can, otherwise move toward them.[/p][p][/p][p]Though something like this could be done entirely in code, systems like this where functionality is implemented via a bunch of smaller building blocks are nice because it can be easier to understand what it’s doing at a glance for all of the developers, and bugs are often more self-contained. If there’s a bug in one of the building blocks, fixing it fixes the issue everywhere that building block is used! If we decide one of the building blocks should function differently, you can change it everywhere at once![/p][p][/p][p]This loops for the entire time the horde monster exists, but other effect chains just happen once. For example, the actual attack in the above effect chain triggers another effect chain, which causes the monster to leap at the player and deal damage to them:[/p][p][/p][p][img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/43170231/5f77d193168130b86a26808dedbc5a7fb1f1d346.png"][/img][/p][p][/p][p]We can see what’s happening in the effect chain in real-time too, which is useful for debugging![/p][p][/p][p][img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/43170231/16fc87bf24fad90395bf9f3e8e704946405a7f72.gif"][/img][/p][p]
We’ve also been replacing some of our older abilities with effect chains. Abilities were originally separated out into many different files (for example, each passive trait had a separate file for both adding and removing it), which was sometimes useful for reusability, but was quite complex and made it difficult to tell what an ability was actually doing. Effect chains are much easier to browse through all at once![/p][p][/p][p][img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/43170231/11c6bc49d55a99e520f62f7961ca575e07f413df.png"][/img][/p][p][i]On the left, an old ability. On the right, that same ability is recreated with an effect chain. Shiny![/i][/p][hr][/hr][p][/p][p]Making useful tools is one of my favorite things to do, so I’ve been having a blast fleshing out this system. One of the big things that’s made it nicer to use is the headers. For example, take a look at this Move step:[/p][p][/p][p][img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/43170231/fe92280cc08cf45be6c62ce4759c2ed32077aa46.png"][/img][/p][p][/p][p]That’s a lot of options! These steps didn’t use to have headers, so you’d need to look through this all to figure out what the step is doing. And when it’s just one step in a set of dozens, it can be difficult to figure out what’s going on.[/p][p]
Now, take a look at this Move step [i]header[/i]![/p][p][/p][p][img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/43170231/165b4b54f2971a0ab37cffe7a17784b7b9e099ea.png"][/img][/p][p][/p][p]One single line that tells you most of what you need to know about the step without expanding it! Much nicer.[/p][p][/p][p]Of course, it can still be hard to parse all this info at a glance, which is why you’ve seen comments underneath the header in many cases. Sometimes it’s easier to just write yourself a note for later.[/p][p][/p][p]I hope this has provided some insight into our development process! And as always:[/p][p][img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/43170231/2653ca6694a08ca715fca6fc427693f0b204aa6e.png"][/img][/p][p]
[/p]

notes.title: DEVLOG #9 THE LEWTON BUS SYSTEM!
notes.content:
Let’s talk about spooky atmosphere! Our encounters are already full of thick fog, horrible creatures, and deadly traps. But we also wanted some more subtle ways to elevate tension. A system of creating apprehension during the quieter moments of the game… So we looked to classic horror cinema- and incorporated a technique known as the [b]Lewton Bus[/b]. A Lewton Bus is a scary moment that (often) turns out to be innocuous- like a cat knocking over a plate with a loud crash.

[h1]The History of the Lewton Bus[/h1]

The Lewton Bus technique is named after 1940s movie producer Val Lewton. The “bus” comes from a famous scene in the 1942 film called Cat People. In the scene, a woman walks alone through a dimly lit street. The tension builds as she is clearly nervous someone is following her or watching her. As the quiet tension reaches its peak, a bus arrives making a sudden loud hiss. The Lewton Bus! There is no actual reveal of danger, it is a clever misdirect that has become extremely popular in horror cinema to this day!

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/43170231/a51bae6f6cee6d577033f2de11858df521560709.gif[/img]
[url=https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=N3vm7UgE0bg][i](Bus Scene from 1942 film - Cat People)[/i][/url]

[h1]Lewton Bus Examples in Film and Video Games[/h1]

A cat has been used in so many Lewton Bus scenes that it has taken on a trope of its own. “It’s just a cat” or a “Cat Scare” has many examples in film. Even in games- like this classic scene from Silent Hill:

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/43170231/8255909ec77afecebc4e12cce398a9b59cd5bf98.gif[/img]
[url=https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=FaxIFlYu66U][i]Cat Jump Scare in Original Silent Hill Game[/i][/url]

Or in films like Alien (1979)

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/43170231/54aa2a3cd0076c412390539b790fcb7d6b68d821.gif[/img]

Shows have even poked fun at this method - like our favorite example in “Community” during this scene where the Lewton Cat-Bus happens several times in a row:

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/43170231/577fe0698c000b0f02c818cbf31d832b23a431c5.gif[/img]
[url=https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=pxauTJpY-hg][i]Community Season 2 Episode 6 “Insane Cat”[/i][/url]

What’s great is how thin a line it is between a Lewton Bus being scary or being funny. Comedy and horror are quite similar in approach, it turns out! Director Jordan Peele famously said: “The difference between horror and comedy is the music.” 

We aim to create tension and anticipation in the audience, and then subvert that expectation with a surprise. In comedy it is a silly surprise, in horror it is a sinister one. In both cases it is a build and release that can feel exhilarating- especially with a group of friends.

[h1]Lewton BEAST![/h1]

We knew we wanted these little moments scattered throughout our game as well! So, we developed a [b]Lewton Bus System[/b] that triggers these jolts based on various gameplay parameters that ensure they happen when the tension has built up and everything else is quiet. 

We reaaally love the technique and how it allows us to be spooky in more tricky ways! The power lies in making the audience feel like they are expecting danger, and then jolt them with a false alarm. It even works on us, the game devs! 

Here we have a very simple example: a garbage can falling down and a rat scurrying away:

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/43170231/41ceff1886170b632ff35496c602399f601e6c18.gif[/img]

And a more sinister examples… a peek from our sewer clown:

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/43170231/f554b4fec2206702276484ab6089061e1b7d38ab.gif[/img]

We are having a blast dreaming up Lewton Bus moments tailored to our hotel and sewer environments—pitching ideas like an elevator bell dinging just before the doors creak open, or a sudden, jarring phone ring echoing from an empty guest room.

Do you have ideas for a Lewton Bus?? Or maybe examples from your favorite games or movies?

Things are ramping up over here - working nonstop to get the game ready! Watch out for cats, cans, clowns, and buses…  and, as always… DEEEEEEP BREATH AAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAA AAAAAAAAAAAAAAA AAAAAAAAAAAAAA AAAAAAAAAAAAAAAA!!!! 

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/43170231/aa6cd74552164a71a2330844dc3e42ae4fad1f2d.gif[/img]

notes.title: DEVLOG #8 THE BACKYARD!
notes.content:
[h1]It’s time for another update![/h1]

This time we want to share the other half of our cozy little clubhouse cove: [b]The Backyard![/b] This is where our little adventurers can choose their loadouts, craft gadgets, upgrade their flashlights, and blow off some steam against cardboard dummies!

[h1]The Backyard[/h1]
No better place to take a deep breath of fresh autumn air! The ideal staging area to prep for some BEAST banishing.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/43170231/62b3baf5ae3713d16eab4f6137d81b96f06d5794.png[/img]

[h1]Cardboard Combat![/h1]
Test your latest abilities, weapons, and attacks on these box beasts! 

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/43170231/8ead3fd9fb78afd0fd80419f84108596026ad1e8.png[/img]

Even Benny will take some swings! But he does secretly wish Camila didn’t draw such convincing faces on them. He prefers to beat up “less intimidating” boxes.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/43170231/21a9fc3ed212954110f93313f0626905beedd638.gif[/img]

[h1]The Tool Shed![/h1]
Watch out mom and dad! This is where the beast hunters hone their weapons. It may not look like much at first, but it houses a real KICK-ARSE ARSENAL!

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/43170231/6387c4f597fdadb1d09789803cf7badda4bc0a07.png[/img]

Here we upgrade our flashlights, unlock powerful batteries, choose special charms with massive magical abilities, and even build traps and gadgets. I think Deacon was jealous of the softball turret at first, but now it’s his favorite tool to deploy! 

Once we’ve upgraded and chosen our favorite charms, it’s time to head out and take down some monsters. With a few batteries and pure childlike imagination, we are unstoppable. We love our little town.

Sure it might be full of deep dark terrors… but you can’t beat the view over Pennybrook.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/43170231/98d47e23be323a606c2c6b3c2624040ed6f90a80.png[/img]

It’s like the ol’ water tower says “Leaf your worries behind!”
Because even when we do lose, we can come back and prepare better for next time.

Stay brave everyone! It can be a dark and scary world, but we all shine bright. So grab each other’s hands and, as always… [i]DEEEEEEP BREATH[/i] AAAAAAAAAAAAAAAA AA AAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAA AAAAAAAAAAAAAAA AAAAAA AAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAA AAAAAAAAAAAAAA AAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAaaaaaaaa!!!!

notes.title: DEVLOG #7 THE CLUBHOUSE!
notes.content:
[h1]Hello Again Intrepid Hunters! [/h1]
We are, as ever, hard at work here in our little lab- cooking up all sorts of monsters and mayhem. However, today’s post will be focused on something a bit cozier. Sure the game is about BEASTS with a capital B…. but these lil heroes also need a place to relax and prepare for their adventure.

So today we are excited to give you a glimpse into the [b]Begone Beast Clubhouse[/b]. Situated just outside of Pennybrook proper, this little slice of heaven gives our adventurers everything they need to stay strong and ready for the battles to come. And really, what better place to set up the clubhouse than Lola’s house! Ate’s gracious grandmama has given in and let us use her basement as the headquarters. [b]Let’s take a look![/b]

[h1]The Clubhouse[/h1]
[b]Talk about putting the BASE into BASEMENT![/b]
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/43170231/b74f599b973f46b3e85c20db9125875fcf370527.png[/img]

We’ve got everything we need in here! 

[h1]The Locker Lineup![/h1]
First off- every beast hunter needs a cubby to call their own. Looks like some are still locked and unused… guess we will have to find some more friends to join the club!

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/43170231/74828e54e03a8d8b2d76c1c2b134c5b7ee4e9df3.gif[/img]


[h1]The Connection Super Highway![/h1]
Lola is also letting us use her [b]STATE OF THE ART COMPUTER!![/b] She says it can even connect to the world wide web - but only if she isn’t on the phone… 

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/43170231/8e3f2cb8f75d5ce66b322172507c39aae101d754.png[/img]

[h1]The Costume Corner![/h1]
We’ve got a fashion stage to try on new clothes and halloween costumes. Sometimes we even have a dance party here… I heard that Deacon even joined in once (I’ll believe it when I see it). We are supposed to keep the room clean, but it just seems to keep getting messy again!

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/43170231/cea35cb5c2b5a124210920046c67d6a1c7449022.png[/img]

[h1]Stairs to the Snack Kitchen[/h1]
Lola barely ever comes downstairs, but we can go upstairs to visit her anytime. She makes all kinds of really good food- and always wants to test new recipes. More food for us! 

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/43170231/93c26fa60b40311e87028b57cf22a6c075cf7327.png[/img]

You can also see our game corner behind the stairs. Benny’s older brothers donated all their old games to us, but I feel like they still come over and play them just as much XD


[h1]Mission Control[/h1]
And finally- here is [b]mission control![/b] This is where we research and plan our BEAST hunts on the overhead projector. Camila got this projector from the local library because they were going to throw it away- but it still works great! It just still says “Property of Pennybrook Books” on the side. 

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/43170231/db0ec3877879b136888a5e33c93e9f906c1f61da.png[/img]

This is just the start- we are even allowed to redecorate it if we want to! There is a furniture catalog to look through.

And there is also the whole [b]BACKYARD[/b] we get to use! But that will be for next time. Can’t wait for you to see the whole clubhouse. 

More updates to come!. And, as always… [i]DEEEEEEP BREATH[/i] AAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAA AAAAAAAAAAAAAAA AAAAAAAAAAAAAA AAAAAAAAAAAAAAAA AAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAA!!!!

notes.title: DEVLOG #006 WEIRD SOUNDS AND WISHLISTS!
notes.content:
Hey there and happy new year to all of you! We are extra happy and thankful to be safe and working with the LA wildfires going on around us. We are facing a bunch of power outages, but luckily none of us are in any danger. 

In other news…

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/43170231/4b01a51a73337201fc96431d59fb32ac2acf9921.gif[/img]

[h1]220K Wishlists! [/h1]
You maniacs took us screaming past 200K wishlists!! This milestone left us speechless and overwhelmed with gratitude. Thanks so much for the love and support. It is hard to express how much it means to us. 

If you would like to get more updates- we expanded our socials recently:

[h1]You can now follow us on Instagram and Bluesky![/h1]
We dipped our toes in the TikTok waters about a month or two ago. And we finally got around to creating an Instagram and Bluesky account over winter break. And yeaa…. They can DEFINITELY use some new friends. Don’t be a stranger – drop by, give us a follow and say hi!

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/43170231/40848ead3150ba783bef9719b9089c95da947e2d.png[/img]

[h1]A Peek at Peekaboo Man’s Signature Sound[/h1]

We are collaborating with our amazing and talented sound partners Sweet Justice Sound to create the Peekaboo Man’s unique voice library. And wow, his personality gives us so much room to play. He is a mischievous writhing mass of flesh… and  his emotions range anywhere from giddy to furious to pouting when things don’t go his way…

Tomas, one of our co-founders, is the voice of the Peekaboo Man. Since we work remotely, the recording sessions take place during the quiet late-night hours, when distractions are minimal and neighbors are fast asleep. In these small hours, Tomas can huddle under a blanket with a microphone and make his strange noises 😂.

But his voice alone doesn't quite do the trick. The audio team took those voice clips, dropped them into their Sweet Justice Sound cauldron and added their magic formula- which in this case was apparently combining Tomas’ voice with the sounds of sea lions, pool noodles… and custard. All blended into a grotesque stew to create a distinct sound for our beloved Peekaboo man. Here is a sneak preview: 

[previewyoutube=SkCmBTsVLkI;full][/previewyoutube]

Mmm… pool noodle custard…

Thanks for reading and, as always *DEEEEEEP BREATH* AAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAA AAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAA!!!!

notes.title: DEVLOG #005 BREATHING LIFE W/ ANIMATION!
notes.content:
Greetings!

Today’s blog post will focus on one of my favorite topics:

[h1]ANIMATION![/h1]

I absolutely love animation and the many ways to think about it. It’s an artform with a lot of hidden depth. There is of course the application of physics and motion- which is challenging itself! Capturing (and heightening) the feeling of impact and weight in a character has soooo many methods and styles. Squashing and stretching, smear frames, hitstops, and all sorts of other methods to capture movement are a fascinating rabbit hole I highly recommend diving into if you are interested in it. As an action game, Begone Beast has had a ton of iteration on how to get actions and reactions to feel good.

There is also [i]acting[/i]- which is easy to overlook. Animation is acting! No matter how good a character’s movements are- they still have to deliver a compelling performance. And that whole acting part is super involved. Diving into specifics of how a character would express a thought or emotion is core to Begone Beast’s characters. We’ve put a particularly large emphasis on ensuring our characters are full of personality and that their actions/expressions are very specific to how each of them think and feel.

And finally- there is the technical animation implementation in games- which is all about creating logic, blending many animations together, and responding to events and inputs from the game to create a sense of responsiveness. Mixing these elements all together is probably my favorite part of game development. Lets take a peek at some of Ate’s animations!

[h1]Core Movement[/h1]

If you are somewhat familiar with game characters- you might have heard of a walk cycle or a run cycle. The way we create a movement set for characters is usually by creating a number of run cycles that blend between speeds and directions to make movement smooth and natural feeling. Begone Beast is no exception! We also use a set of run cycles to create a movement set. However- this didn’t quite feel like enough for me. There was something that felt too… “cycle-y” and I wasn’t initially sure why. I wanted our characters to feel fidgety, anxious, like kids! And one of the best ways I found achieved this effect was to alternate between a set of cycles that hold the flashlight two handed, and a set that holds the flashlight one handed. While simple- the effect really transformed the character from feeling like an animation, to feeling a lot more natural!

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/43170231/41d120126e420fca83e58e4889d546db1e8d02e3.gif[/img]

[h1]Strafing Movement[/h1]
This also works across all of our strafe animations. Here you can see how Ate switches from 1 to 2 hands while also moving in a full 360 strafe set of running animations.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/43170231/4dc08c1c9169ee699f9856919e88892d285e6f01.gif[/img]

Here is what the animations look like in our logic tree. Four animations blend between each other for each movement set.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/43170231/d91aacb290477b02584009f248e0fda7edcee5b4.gif[/img]

[h1]Leading with the Eyes[/h1]
But that’s not all! The faces of our characters are a HUMUNGOUS part of them feeling alive. I did a test to have the eyes dart toward any new joystick direction. This turned out to be a really awesome small touch that breathed life into the characters. Giving them a sense of intent:

You can see it in this gif- as you change inputs Ate’s eyes will dart toward the new direction:

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/43170231/a24488e2e10096842971834f40c4b4b08fca4942.gif[/img]

[h1]Blinks and More Blinks![/h1]
Layered over all of the animations is a set of eye darts and blinks that help tie everything together. Animators love talking about blinks! There are so many different kinds, so many different ways to animate them. I particularly love half-blinks (which you can see included in our blink set). I also love to really involve the whole face in a blink- you can see how Ate’s face squishes a bit with each blink- her blinks even make her bun wiggle! Haha! 

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/43170231/3cf8168380b8278f3db3bf5d79cc86269778eca1.gif[/img]

[h1]Face Blend Shapes[/h1]
Our characters achieve this level of detail in their facial expressions because their faces are animated directly on the model vertices rather than using a traditional animation rig. Face rigs are typically very high bone count or else they lack precise control (especially if you have lots of very different faces!) but I just HAD to have full control over very big expressions. So hand modeling every expression has really allowed me to create much more expressive faces. The animation of these are driven by a switchboard of sliders - its fun to watch them all move around:

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/43170231/0de4c641047af58ae283067671b9185460a32f05.gif[/img]

There is sooooo much more to talk about with animation- but I’ve already gone on too long! This will have to be a multi-part post. Ok one more thing! Each player character has a “personality flourish” animation that they play after big attacks and combos. This turned out to be a great way to sneak little bits of extra personality into gameplay. Ate’s is absolutely maniacal:

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/43170231/a5de71ef2e5a630e77f4dc500b6030a712f1d829.gif[/img]

Ok ok! I will share even more about animation soon. There is sooo much more to talk about, but I gotta get back to work! Thanks so much for joining me on this journey and, as always *DEEEEEEP BREATH* AAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAA AAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAA!!!!

-Tomas

notes.title: DEVLOG #004 MOM
notes.content:
Hello everyone! 

I’m Clarissa, one of the co-founders and engineers at Tandemi, as well as the architect behind our Map Outline Maker, or MOM. MOM is responsible for generating unique map layouts on each playthrough. She works together with the Dynamic AI Director, or DAD, (more info on DAD in a future post!) to dynamically spawn monsters and obstacles tailored to each experience with your friends - because… they love you of course!

MOM didn’t become awesome overnight. We went through what felt like countless iterations of procedural generation architecture over the course of development- and there will surely be countless more iterations in the future!

When I first started building MOM, I was eager to learn pathfinding algorithms to build our first maps. (this kicked my butt btw… but shaped me into being a better programmer). I worked within a 2D grid and placed big and small squares that represented bespoke segments in a level. These handcrafted rooms would represent different points of interest depending on the environment. For example - The Sewer’s trash compactor and generator room, or The Hotel’s ballroom or bedroom suite. I used both A* and Dijkstra’s pathfinding algorithms to create intricate maps that included alternative routes and dead ends. The configurations of maps were endless! 

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/43170231/2d668ab4f995bdb1cbc6e66dc917bc892ca2043f.png[/img]
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/43170231/3d340e4a57275f1ad9486fa9a85237488da8c275.png[/img]

[i]Above are the early stages of auto generated levels. This early algorithm was limited by the bounds of a preset grid, and could only support a few larger points of interest. But it was already fun to run through![/i]

As MOM evolved, we found ways to increase variety while also giving art and design more flexibility to handcraft points of interest. We currently use what we call a "stitching" method where we "stitch" segments together, and no longer have the bounds of a grid. Artists know to create individual segments that will seamlessly connect to any segment which ultimately forms a cohesive level of any dimension.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/43170231/962f49dcbe330fadb2f24dce3b6c20baaa0705ba.png[/img]
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/43170231/798f478db1e8e2c2f1c3c8077974e12a9cb27db0.gif[/img]
[i]Above is an example of our current “stitch method”. Shown is the workings of MOM generating a unique level. MOM also customizes the decor and content inside a segment. Here are some wall variations in the sewer that can be picked randomly in the level.[/i]

MOM is designed to be flexible, allowing elements of any size to be stitched together. These pieces are quickly placed, arranged, and rearranged to ensure a fully navigable level. MOM even ensures the monsters have paths to invade the level. She can customize the decor, functionality, and content inside the map as well. MOM is unstoppable! She is a free spirit and capable of making on occasion some “WTF is that?”- looking maps. My job as the engineer is to expand her capabilities of creating engaging and unpredictable levels.

MOM also plays a vital role for the developers of Begone Beast in everyday production — making each playthrough surprising even for the devs, and allowing artists and designers the tools to easily make huge impacts on the level design with small tweaks. We are thrilled to introduce MOM to you soon and hope you will love her as much as we do!

Thanks for reading and, as always *DEEEEEEP BREATH* AAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAA!!!!

- C

notes.title: DEVLOG #003: THANK YOU FOR 125k WISHLISTS!!
notes.content:
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/43170231/ebc0d6a03265c2a0188e6f5482f0f7a1ea511449.jpg[/img]

Wow wow wow! You absolute legends!! 125k wishlists and counting! There are no words. We are just over the moon… nay- Over the stars!! [b]C[/b]annot believe it! The BEASTS are quaking in their boots! Haha! We may have to make them… stronger.

We can’t wait to be able to share more of the game to you. Our lil dev team is chuggin right along! [b]A[/b]t the moment, Tandemi is a four person team (with a few helpful contractors). We are playtesting daily - putting our cute and cuddly little heroes through their paces. These courageous little misfits are tirelessly taking on the terrors of the dark.. Although they take their fair share of wallopings as well. 

We are eager to share more gameplay with you all soon! In the [b]M[/b]eantime, we’d like to share some of the process behind the scenes of our latest trailer:

TRAILER STORYBOARDS VS FINAL 

STORYBOARDS CLIP 1
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/43170231/49a93b4027ad0d9f6dc9d3e12f055e33f022db2b.gif[/img]

[url=https://youtube.com/shorts/TV3Q6GiYKj8?si=8vq00nChJbY9hJ2V]CLIP 1 on Youtube[/url]

Here is a comparison of the storyboard art and final animation for our opening sequence. The storyboards were done by a fantastic contract artist. But there were some boards [b]I[/b] drew at the veeeerrry beginning- which you can see below:

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/43170231/27054e39f2e5fe1deaecf1b4b6c55cf5a38171ae.gif[/img]

The models/rigs in the trailer are our in-game rigs. I wanted to avoid making whole face rigs for each character because of performance, bone count, complexity, all those things are why we don’t see as much polished face animation in game assets. So instead we sculpt each face, which has been a great lightweight method of getting the results we want. These little maniacs have to have their expressions just right! 

STORYBOARDS CLIP 2
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/43170231/041a539ef90ad7daa0630738310699dec1babbc7.gif[/img]
[i]That’s odd… the hands usually get off on the second floor[/i]

[url=https://youtube.com/shorts/cZW3UnbC7ME?si=y-9kBrsERK0cZj_6]CLIP 2 on Youtube[/url]

The E[b]L[/b]evator sequence! So much of our game is little love letters and re-imaginings of our favorite horror/spooky stuff. It was my dream to drop our intrepid mini-adventurers into an homage to the great Overlook Hotel. So neat to bring it into the trailer (and the game).

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/43170231/7a840b50021872adffdaec708f02a048936c85a5.png[/img]

And yes- the hands were all hand animated. It was quite an intimidating shot to set up- but we really wanted to capture the feeling of the blood elevator, as well as the feeling of the hordes you will be seeing in Begone Beast. (Hands won’t be the only type of horde, btw!)

STORYBOARDS CLIP 3
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/43170231/7346590c02256a9baedacaaae86dbd4616eb18aa.gif[/img]

[url=https://youtube.com/shorts/13d1crfDF1w?si=5xGI3FQvjRXroB4V]CLIP 3 on Youtube[/url]

Ah the Peekaboo Man. Our own horrible flesh blob. We can’t wait to show more of him. And I snuck in a little homage to the Mines of Moria. 

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/43170231/ff7dbcd8cede4fe04f3530642bfbd1d9c57d780e.png[/img]
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/43170231/5e28371eefc1608eef8b25b1b42ee0e751e46520.png[/img]
[i]And they call it a mine![/i]

WHAT IS THE FROG’S NAME??

Many of you have been asking who is our delightful Frog mage? She’s a bit shy, but is a brilliant academic (and an adept baton twirler!) She also happens to be crushing hard on a certain other member of the group. We’ve got the other character’s names: Deacon, Benny, and of course Ate. I’m not supposed to share our frog’s name yet… but I guess if her name was to be expertly hidden within this blog post somewhere, noone would be the wiser. Just a thought!

Alright all you fine folks! HUGE thanks again for those wishlists. Let’s goooo! Keep posted for some meaty updates coming soon. And, as always [i]*DEEEEEEP BREATH*[/i] [b]A[/b]AAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAA AAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAA!!!!

notes.title: DEVLOG #002 REACTIONS & REMEMBERING
notes.content:
[b]Hey party people! [/b]

As we embrace the crisp delights of autumn, we're still basking in the warmth of our reception at Gamescom and the wild reactions we got! We're also taking a moment to reflect on our game development journey. PAX West just concluded, and while we weren’t able to attend this year, PAX holds a special place in our hearts as it was pivotal in our start on this game dev adventure. Read more below!

[h1]GAMESCOM REACTION HIGHLIGHTS![/h1]

You’ve been incredibly kind to us these past two weeks! We were absolutely floored by the reactions to our latest trailer. Thank you so much to everyone who watched! It was truly amazing to see it air during Gamescom Opening Night Live. We were especially captivated by all the streams that reacted to our trailer. Moments like these remind us why we’re making games in the first place.

Since we’ve never experienced anything quite like this, we decided to put together a highlights reel. It was tough to choose from all the fantastic reactions and streams, but we did our best to compile a collection of some of the most fun ones. You can check it out on YouTube here:

[previewyoutube=ShIu4QFuF-4;full][/previewyoutube]

Huge thanks to all the content creators who took the time to share reactions. The whole thing has really refueled us for the work ahead. We are more motivated than ever!

[h1]PAX WEST THROWBACK[/h1]

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/43170231/325afb01c45aeb9b96188f5fdf105e1921c83c6b.jpg[/img]

Preparing for PAX West 2022 was simultaneously nerve-racking and exciting since this was the very first time we were showcasing Begone Beast to players that weren’t industry people or immediate family members. Ahead of time, we prepared these snack bags as a “thanks for playtesting!” for attendees that playtested the demo. 

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/43170231/66a71b59ae4817419dead9804e738ab3d4f6eec5.png[/img]

Snacks have always been core to the gameplay (more on that in future posts!) and wanted to incorporate it in our playtesting experience. There is something uniquely wholesome and childlike about having a snack bag- as well as feeling a bit like you are on an adventure. Clarissa’s brother was living in Seattle at the time and we shipped 3 huge boxes full of snacks and supplies so that he could drive it over to the convention center, while we flew from Los Angeles. 

We were set up amongst other indie developers who were the best neighbors! Hydes: Haunt & Seek by Smol Games and 30XX by Batterystaple Games. Our booth design was basically just a huge TV- The goal was to get people seeing it for the first time to say “What the f*** is that??!” And I think we did a pretty good job accomplishing that. It was Clarissa’s brother (the same one who drove the snacks) that had the idea for the demon horn light rope haha!

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/43170231/144aac4bcf55a053aa87281ffcdc0771e04163ba.png[/img]

One of the many highlights of our PAX West demo was the head-wobble feature in our character selection screen. It had a simple red background. Once you locked in your character, you can bobble their head with the joystick and scream with the buttons. We have since changed the character select- but we’ve preserved the head-bobble mode in other fun ways. But that will be for another post!

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/43170231/208d56cee04be7fa3033d2c08d425180f5d63929.gif[/img]

So again- Huge thanks for all the great feedback. We will have much more to share soon! And, as always *DEEEEP BREATH* AAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAA AAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAA!!!!

notes.title: DEV-LOG #001: HOW IT ALL BEGONE!
notes.content:
[h2]Hello World![/h2]
My name is Tomas. I am an animator. I am also one of two cofounders of Tandemi- the studio making Begone Beast! The other cofounder is Clarissa (my partner, my wife, and programmer extraordinaire!). And… 

We are absolutely thrilled to share a new trailer with you that was just shown at Gamescom! 

[h3]BEGONE BEAST Early Access Announcement Trailer[/h3]
[previewyoutube=zrqZ91wqPEg;full][/previewyoutube]

But we are even MORE thrilled to announce we are headed to Early Access in 2025. It’s great to finally start sharing what we’ve been working on! Nevertheless, the MOST thrilling thing of all is that YOU are here reading this. So awesome! We will be regularly posting updates here every few weeks so stick around if you want to learn more!

[h2]In the Begonning[/h2]
First lets talk about how the idea for Begone Beast came about. Clarissa and I love going to Haunted Houses. We go each year to Halloween Horror Nights with a bunch of friends & fam. The group of us turns into this big bundle of scared, giggling, screaming scaredy-cats eagerly running from every fake chainsaw and masked madman – only stopping to stuff ourselves with ice cream and hot dogs. It’s weirdly wholesome (especially considering all the fake blood and gore). It’s precisely this odd spooky wholesomeness that sparked our journey to make Begone Beast.

At first the game was just a collection of inspiration and references. We wanted something full of delightful silliness, but grounded in some really scary places. We wanted a Luigi’s Mansion as if it were created by Stephen King.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/43170231/1d7a28ccde3bddca58479ffd6d862871d43f8906.jpg[/img]
[i]As a game developer, it’s all work and all play![/i]

It needed to be scary… but kinda fun-scary with lots of snack breaks. Something equal parts Overcooked! and Left 4 Dead. Topped off with the earnest wonder of Calvin and Hobbes… and a bit of that surreal autumnal coziness in Over the Garden Wall. And so we poured all these inspirations into a big cauldron and saw if anything sparked

[h2]Our First Prototype![/h2]
It wasn’t until we made our first prototype that we felt the spark. In it you played as a little bear boy looking for ghosts and ghouls. It was a glimpse at something we wanted to keep working on. We called that first bear-bones prototype “Ghost Patrol”. It wasn’t much, but there was something special about it.

[previewyoutube=jd2dU44DBVk;full][/previewyoutube]
[i]Our first playable prototype “Ghost Patrol”[/i]

This short demo would eventually turn into the game we are building today! It was a creepy-cute mix that we just couldn’t stop thinking about.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/43170231/f711c9cc10bd56af7d59e8bdf67fb15b5c54a7cc.png[/img]
[i]“Bear Boy” would later become Benny- the first playable character in Begone Beast[/i]


[h2]FINDING OUR LEAD CHARACTER[/h2]

There was a really specific turning point when the game really started to take shape. As a bit of a joke, I decided to try and create a playable character based on my fellow cofounder Clarissa herself. They say to make what you know, right? Well I had known Clarissa almost 10 years at that point. Her exaggerated expressions, her brash boldness, and her propensity to scream. But I wasn’t prepared for how much I would love playing as her.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/43170231/e8654f6132546c3380d31655df016f0570f4cc0f.gif[/img]
[i]“Ate” pronounced “Ah-tay” has accumulated a whole array of custom expressions.[/i]

Well it turned out that basing a character on someone I knew was actually really effective. I immediately knew how she should move, attack, talk, and scream! We had found our main character and named her “Ate”(pronounced “Ah-tay”). And while Clarissa may have been the inspiration, Ate soon became a reflection of Clarissa’s whole extended family.

More updates coming soon!
After we made Ate, the other characters started to fall into place. We had our starting roster of Begoners! And so we turned our focus to the cast of monsters and BEASTS… but we’ll leave that for another time.

If you’ve read this far, you have my thanks. We’d love to have you join playtesting once we get started. Stay-tuned for more updates! And as always [deep breath] AAAAAAAAAAAA AAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAA  AAAAAAAAAAAAAA!!!

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/43170231/cbe514a3190c2996e9d5d85c2eba1ce6d9cbde1a.gif[/img]
